Read /Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec4/luna/package.md. It holds image section 4 (Tutmak: kendini tutan, tutulan ve elini tutan) of the frozen surah commentary of surah 103: the Arabic text of the ayat concerned, the Turkish
commentary written on them, the words/roots/branch labels recorded in the frozen surah commentary, and the
whole surah in Arabic. The selected commentary defines your scope; the other inputs supply context.

Find, from the Hebrew Bible, the New Testament, and the Jewish and Christian literature around them (Targum,
Mishnah, Talmud, midrash, pseudepigrapha, Christian apocrypha, Church Fathers, Syriac homilies), every text an
advanced reader of this commentary should have beside it. Judge each text on what it says in its own place, not
on resemblance of a word. Weigh at least:

- paralel: the same figure, scene or story told in the other scripture;
- motif: a shared image, formula, liturgical act or ethical motif without a shared story;
- karsi_anlati: the Qur'an tells it differently, corrects or answers it; the difference is the point;
- soydas: a Hebrew, Aramaic or Syriac cognate of a key word of these ayat and how the other scripture uses it;
- yorum_gelenegi: Jewish or Christian interpretation of a parallel text that changes what the parallel means.

Before grading, work through every distinct scene, object, action, relation, formula and secondary sense
actually developed in the commentary, including any v16 augment additions. Recall direct formulations, repeated
occurrences, nonlexical parallels, relevant reversals and interpretive traditions. Do not let the title, first
scene or already quoted passages stand in for the whole page. For a Buluşmalar section, consider the particular
meetings between images its prose develops. Root/branch labels are not dictionary definitions, evidence of
cognacy or permission to import an undeveloped sense. Do this review internally; output only candidate rows.

Use the package's Semitic root table: for every Arabic root it lists, recall how the corresponding Hebrew or
Aramaic root is used across the Hebrew Bible, passages that play on the same consonants, and passages whose
wording shows a difference from what the ayah says. Propose such passages as soydas (shared root), motif,
paralel or karsi_anlati as fits, and name the basis in `basis` (the root, and whether it is the table's sound
correspondence or your own recollection). Same consonants with an unrelated sense are not a connection.

Every explanation must identify a particular detail or claim in the commentary, the corresponding detail in
the candidate's own context, and what the relationship adds. Shared vocabulary, a broad religious theme or
the same speaker alone is insufficient. Do not invent imagery that neither text supports. A shared word is
not required. Preserve indirect, secondary and contrary readings with a concrete connection; do not choose
one preferred reading. A parallel is not a dependence: say what the texts share, not who borrowed.

Check the speaker, addressee, action, negation and verse boundary in remembered context. Name a neighbouring
verse separately when its own contribution is necessary; proximity alone does not qualify it. Keep Hebrew,
Aramaic, Syriac and Greek quotations short and specific to the cited passage and witness. If exact wording or
numbering is uncertain, explain the connection and uncertainty in English instead of reconstructing a quote.
Label roots, dictionary forms and wording from the source commentary explicitly. Never combine verses into
one quotation. Distinguish WLC's written/ketiv stream from qere and other readings; name another witness when
you rely on it. Discovery is memory-only: the later verifier will open the actual texts and check your claims.

Include every candidate meeting this standard. There is no target list length. Strong means a direct,
specific correspondence, including a secondary feature developed in the prose. Medium means a specific
correspondence with an explicit interpretive bridge. Weak means a plausible, specific connection whose
uncertainty you identify; it still cannot be generic. Counter-narrative is a relationship kind, not weaker
confidence. Model agreement and a follow-up origin never make a claim verified.

Write one TSV row per distinct connection with exactly six tab-separated fields:

strength	tradition	kind	ref	basis	short_explanation

strength: strong, medium, weak. tradition: tevrat (Hebrew Bible and Jewish literature) or incil (New Testament and
Christian literature). kind: paralel, motif, karsi_anlati, soydas, yorum_gelenegi. ref: for the Hebrew Bible and
the New Testament an edition-qualified OSIS reference, one verse per row, no ranges
(WLC:Gen.22.2, WLC:Ps.1.3, SBLGNT:Matt.6.5; consecutive verses on their own rows).
Use Hebrew WLC numbering for Hebrew Bible candidates and SBLGNT numbering for New Testament candidates;
do not silently transfer English/KJV verse numbers. For other works give the work and its place as a reader

Genesis Rabbah 56:1; Berakhot 60b; Ephrem, Hymns on Paradise 5:6; Protevangelium of James 8). basis: the words,
scene or motif that carries the link, in a few words. Strongest first. Keep distinct reasons or link kinds for
one passage in separate rows; exact repeated connections are unnecessary. Do not regrade an existing row.
The handoff groups references but preserves each distinct connection for an individual verdict.

## Frozen commentary (Turkish)

Asr da sabır da tutmak, alıkoymak diye açıklanır: {ar:العصر الحبس, tr:el-asru'l-habs, gloss:asr, alıkoymaktır, source:"ع ص ر,B006"}, {ar:الصبر حبس النفس عن الجزع, tr:es-sabru habsu'n-nefsi ani'l-ceza', gloss:sabır, nefsi feryattan alıkoymaktır, source:"ص ب ر,B001"}. Sahnede birkaç tür tutma vardır. Kişi kendini tutar: {ar:صبرت نفسي أي حبستها, tr:sabartu nefsî, gloss:nefsimi tuttum, source:"ص ب ر,B001"}; oruç bu tutmanın bir türüdür {ar:سمي الصوم صبرا لكونه كالنوع له, tr:summiye's-savmu sabran, gloss:oruç, sabrın bir türü olduğu için sabır diye anıldı, source:"ص ب ر,B015"}. Tersi de aynı kelimeyle söylenir: başkası tarafından tutulan, ölüme bağlanan esir {ar:المصبورة المحبوسة على الموت, tr:el-masbûra, gloss:ölüme alıkonmuş olan, source:"ص ب ر,B002"}, {ar:الصبر نصب الإنسان للقتل, tr:es-sabru nasbu'l-insâni li'l-katl, gloss:sabır, insanın öldürülmek için dikilmesidir, source:"ص ب ر,B002"}, zorla yemin ettirilen adam {ar:صبرت يمينه أي حلفته, tr:sabartu yemînehû, gloss:onu yemine zorladım, source:"ص ب ر,B002"}. Üçüncü tür eldir: veremediğini tutan el {ar:فلان عاصر إذا كان ممسكا, tr:fulânun âsirun, gloss:eli sıkı olana âsir denir, source:"ع ص ر,B006"}, babanın oğlunun malını ondan alıkoyması {ar:يعتصر الوالد على ولده في ماله, tr:ya'tasiru'l-vâlidu alâ veledih, gloss:baba çocuğunun malını ondan tutar, source:"ع ص ر,B006"}. Evde tutulan genç kız {ar:المعصر ساعة تطمث أي تحيض لأنها تحبس في البيت, tr:el-mu'sır, gloss:ilk aybaşında evde tutulan kız, source:"ع ص ر,B009"} ve kabuğunda korunan tahıl {ar:مأخوذ من العصر وهو الحرز أي تحرز في غلفه, tr:min el-asr ve huve'l-hirz, gloss:korunak anlamındaki asrdan; kabuğunda korunur, source:"ع ص ر,B010"} da bu ailededir. En uç ters çevrilme ise ateşe karşı cüret olarak sabırdır: {ar:الصبر الجرأة ومنه فما أصبرهم على النار, tr:es-sabru'l-cur'a, gloss:sabır cüret anlamına da gelir, source:"ص ب ر,B013"}.

İkinci ayetteki insan, tutulmuş olanın adıyla anılan insandır: ölüme dikilen "insan" bu kelimeyle söylenir. Üçüncü ayet ise sabrın öteki yüzünü, kişinin kendi nefsini tutmasını birbirine tavsiye edilen şey yapar. Düz bir anlatım bu iki tutmanın aynı kelimede durduğunu göstermez: ya kendini tutarsın ya da tutulursun. Kur'an insanın tutamayan hâlini aynı kalıpla anlatır: {ar:إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ خُلِقَ هَلُوعًا, tr:inne'l-insâne hulika helû'â, gloss:insan pek tez canlı yaratıldı, source:70:19}, {ar:إِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ جَزُوعًۭا, tr:izâ messehu'ş-şerru cezû'â, gloss:kötülük dokununca feryat eder, source:70:20}, {ar:وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلْخَيْرُ مَنُوعًا, tr:ve izâ messehu'l-hayru menû'â, gloss:iyilik dokununca esirger, source:70:21}, ardından istisna: {ar:إِلَّا ٱلْمُصَلِّينَ, tr:ille'l-musallîn, gloss:namaz kılanlar hariç, source:70:22}. Feryat sabrın zıddıdır {ar:الصبر نقيض الجزع, tr:es-sabru nakîdu'l-ceza', gloss:sabır feryadın karşıtıdır, source:"ص ب ر,B001"}; esirgeyen el de âsirin elidir. Aynı insan {ar:لَّأَمْسَكْتُمْ خَشْيَةَ ٱلْإِنفَاقِ ۚ وَكَانَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ قَتُورًۭا, tr:le-emsektum haşyete'l-infâk ve kâne'l-insânu katûrâ, gloss:harcamaktan korkup tutardınız; insan pek cimridir, source:17:100} diye de anılır. Başkası tarafından tutulma Kur'an'da hesaba bağlanır: {ar:كُلُّ نَفْسٍۭ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ, tr:kullu nefsin bimâ kesebet rahîne, gloss:her nefis kazandığına karşılık rehindir, source:74:38}.

Ters çevrilmiş sabır Kur'an'da kötü alışverişle aynı ayettedir: {ar:أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشْتَرَوُا۟ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ بِٱلْهُدَىٰ, tr:ulâike'llezîne'şteravu'd-dalâlete bi'l-hudâ, gloss:onlar hidayete karşılık sapıklığı satın alanlardır, source:2:175}, {ar:فَمَآ أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ, tr:fe-mâ asbarahum ale'n-nâr, gloss:ateşe ne kadar dayanıklılar (ne cüretkârlar), source:2:175}. Beklemek olarak sabır ise Peygamber'e söylenir: {ar:فَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌۭ, tr:fasbir li-hukmi rabbike ve lâ tekun ke-sâhibi'l-hût, gloss:Rabbinin hükmüne sabret; balık sahibi gibi olma, o tıkanmış hâlde seslenmişti, source:68:48}; bekleyen, gözetim altındadır: {ar:وَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا, tr:vasbir li-hukmi rabbike fe-inneke bi-a'yuninâ, gloss:Rabbinin hükmüne sabret, sen gözlerimizin önündesin, source:52:48}. Tutma bir topluluğa da genişler: {ar:ٱصْبِرُوا۟ وَصَابِرُوا۟ وَرَابِطُوا۟, tr:isbirû ve sâbirû ve râbitû, gloss:sabredin, sabırda yarışın, bağlı durun, source:3:200}.

strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Thess.5.14	patience with the weak	The commentary makes sabr something believers enjoin on one another; Paul tells the congregation to encourage the fainthearted, help the weak, and be patient with everyone. Its context makes patience a shared practice toward vulnerable people.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.9	doing good and not tiring	The commentary pairs righteous action with reciprocal counsel to patience; Paul joins not growing weary in doing good with the promise of harvest for those who do not give up. The link makes ethical work a practice sustained through waiting.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.25	mutual encouragement as the Day approaches	The commentary's repeated tawāṣaw is reciprocal counsel; Hebrews tells believers to encourage one another, increasingly as they see the Day approaching. It locates mutual support inside an expectation that calls for endurance.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.16.32	rule of spirit over conquest	The commentary glosses sabr as holding oneself back from panic; Proverbs ranks slowness to anger above military might and ruling one's spirit above capturing a city. It makes self-restraint a form of strength rather than domination.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.25.28	self-control as a wall	The commentary contrasts the self-held person with the person held by others; Proverbs likens a person without self-control to a breached city without walls. The image makes restraint protection against becoming capturable.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.29.11	venting versus holding back	The commentary's B001 gloss says sabr holds the self back from panic or outcry; Proverbs contrasts a fool who vents his whole spirit with a wise person who stills it. This is a direct wisdom parallel for keeping an impulse from spilling out.
strong	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Mishnah Avot 4:1	subduing one's inclination	The commentary presents sabr as self-restraint; Ben Zoma interprets Proverbs' ruler of his spirit as the truly mighty person who subdues his inclination. This Jewish reading turns the proverb's city-conquest comparison into inward mastery.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.11.24	withholding and poverty	The commentary calls the withholding hand miserly and cites the human who holds back from spending; Proverbs says one who withholds what should be given comes to want. It makes retention itself a path into the loss the surah announces.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Luke.12.20	stored harvest and life demanded	The commentary joins the withholding of wealth to the soul pledged for what it earns; in Jesus' parable the rich fool enlarges his barns, then has his life demanded that night. strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.2.15	enslavement to fear of death	The commentary calls the human captive to death; Hebrews says people are held in lifelong slavery through fear of death, and its surrounding argument presents Christ as liberator. strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.53.7	held for slaughter, silent under oppression	The commentary's B002 gloss describes the one held for death; Isaiah's servant is oppressed and led like a lamb to slaughter, yet does not open his mouth. strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.2.23	no threat while suffering	The commentary sets the person held for killing beside the one who holds himself back; Peter says Christ did not retaliate or threaten when suffering, but entrusted himself to the just judge. It reads restraint under injustice as chosen trust rather than mere helplessness.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.27.2	bound and delivered to the governor	The commentary's B002 gloss is a person detained for death; Matthew says the leaders bound Jesus and delivered him to Pilate, leading into the execution narrative. This gives the passive, externally held figure a concrete Passion setting.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.22.9	binding before a near-sacrifice	The commentary describes al-maṣbūra as one kept for death; in the Aqedah Abraham binds Isaac and places him on the altar before the killing is stopped. strong	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Genesis Rabbah 56:8	Isaac's willing binding	The commentary's B002 image is a person bound for killing; Genesis Rabbah has Isaac ask to be bound securely so that he will not flinch and invalidate the offering. strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jon.2.3	Jonah's distress-call	The commentary cites Jonah as the prophet who called out while constricted and warns against his response; WLC Jonah records his prayer beginning with a call from distress in the fish, followed by God's answer. strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.2.10	receiving adversity without speech against God	The commentary glosses sabr as holding oneself back from panic or lament; after Job's losses he refuses his wife's counsel to curse God and does not sin with his lips. medium	incil	yorum_gelenegi	SBLGNT:Jas.5.11	Job's endurance and the Lord's outcome	The commentary treats patience as waiting for God's judgment; James names Job's endurance and points readers to the Lord's compassionate purpose. strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.33.18	the eye of God on those who wait	The commentary quotes the prophet told to be patient because he is in God's eyes; this psalm places the LORD's eye on those who hope in his steadfast love. strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.130.5	waiting in the divine word	The commentary explains sabr as waiting for the Lord's decree; the psalmist waits for the LORD and hopes in his word. It gives the waiting stance a textual object and a first-person prayer form.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.36	endurance before receiving the promise	The commentary calls sabr waiting for the Lord's judgment; Hebrews says endurance is needed after doing God's will in order to receive what was promised.
